issues.reason: The NL requires an ongoing cooking-time display/update behavior in ReadytoCook, but the closed model has no action on this state. No explicit lifecycle phase (entry, do, or exit) is stated in the NL text or binding hints; the phrase 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated' is generic state-description wording, not an exact phase indicator. S4 cannot be executed without a phase, so the claim is preserved as predicate-null W1.
issues.requirement_quote: where the cooking time is displayed and updated
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The cooking-time display and update may be considered implicit operational semantics of the ReadytoCook state rather than requiring an explicit action annotation in the FCSTM formalism.
issues.title: ReadytoCook state lacks required cooking-time display and update action

issues.basis: NL segment NL6 states 'canceling or updating the cooking time' as an effect of the Cancel action; FCSTM transition:line:27 effects field is empty array; inspection-equivalent facts confirm effects=[] for this transition.
issues.expected: The Cancel transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem should carry an effect that cancels or updates the cooking time.
issues.observed: Transition line:27 (ReadytoCook → DoorShutWithItem on Cancel) has effects=[] in the closed model; no effect is declared on this transition.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires an effect on this specific transition, but the closed model declares no effect on transition:line:27. Transition-effect claims are preserved as predicate-null W1 candidates per frozen-predicate routing rules since no registered predicate directly checks transition effect content.
issues.requirement_quote: canceling or updating the cooking time
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The cooking-time reset may be considered implicitly discharged by leaving the ReadytoCook state rather than requiring an explicit effect annotation on the transition itself.
issues.title: Cancel transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem lacks required cooking-time cancel or update effect

issues.basis: NL segment NL7 normative statement 'Upon entering the Cooking state, the timer starts'; FCSTM state:Cooking:line:16 has no actions; reference inspection facts show actions count=0; the phrase 'Upon entering' explicitly identifies the entry lifecycle phase.
issues.expected: The Cooking state should have an entry action that starts the timer upon state entry.
issues.observed: The closed model's Cooking state (state:Cooking:line:16) has no lifecycle actions declared; reference inspection facts confirm zero actions in the entire model.
issues.reason: The NL normative statement explicitly says 'Upon entering the Cooking state, the timer starts,' providing all three S4 inputs: state=Cooking, phase=entry (from 'Upon entering'), and action=timer starts. The closed model has no entry action on Cooking, so the required action is missing.
issues.requirement_quote: Upon entering the Cooking state, the timer starts.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The timer start could alternatively be modeled as a transition effect on the incoming Start transition (transition:line:29) rather than as a state entry action, though the NL explicitly frames it as occurring 'upon entering' the state.
issues.title: Cooking state lacks required entry action to start timer

issues.basis: NL segment NL8 states 'opening the door stops the timer and the system transitions to DoorOpenWithItem'; FCSTM transition:line:30 effects field is empty array; inspection-equivalent facts confirm effects=[] for this transition.
issues.expected: The Door_Opened transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem should carry an effect that stops the timer.
issues.observed: Transition line:30 (Cooking → DoorOpenWithItem on Door_Opened) has effects=[] in the closed model; no effect is declared on this transition.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires a timer-stop effect on this specific transition, but the closed model declares no effect on transition:line:30. Transition-effect claims are preserved as predicate-null W1 candidates per frozen-predicate routing rules.
issues.requirement_quote: opening the door stops the timer
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The timer stop may be considered implicitly discharged by exiting the Cooking state rather than requiring an explicit effect annotation on the transition.
issues.title: Door_Opened transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem lacks required timer-stop effect
